method: Enumerated pending entries in all inventory partitions; screened source spans/opcode families for FP, vector, CFG, and absent property semantics; checked candidate spans against the pinned source. These are recommendations only; inventory files were not changed.

items.source_evidence: foldSelectOpOp accepts any unary CastInst (`TI->isCast()`), requires matching input types, then creates a select over cast inputs and recreates the cast. That includes FP casts and pointer/integer cast cases in addition to scalar integer casts.
items.capability_gap: Puddle select interprets integer operands only; FP cast opcodes/poisoned-float semantics are unavailable; pointer-result selects are unsupported and pointer cast interpretation is only restricted (capability guide lines 100-116). Vector cast/select cases lack an elementwise proof interface (lines 166-173).
items.recommended_scope: Keep the scalar integer cast specialization pending. Record blockers only for FP-cast, pointer-valued select/cast, and vector variants; do not classify the entire source branch unsupported. Also note the current inventory match-opcode list should account for the source’s generic cast set if it is intended to enumerate all matched cast opcodes.

items.source_evidence: commonCastTransforms composes an eliminable two-cast chain according to LLVM cast-pair/type and pointer-size checks. Inventory match/rewrite opcodes include FP casts, ptrtoint/inttoptr, and integer casts.
items.capability_gap: Puddle has no semantics for FP cast operations or poisoned FP; pointer cast support is limited to 64-bit ptrtoint/inttoptr and does not supply arbitrary LLVM DataLayout/address-space semantics (capability guide lines 100-124).
items.recommended_scope: Retain scalar integer cast-pair cases pending. Restrict the blocker to pairs requiring FP semantics or pointer width/address-space/layout behaviors outside the documented RV64 subset.

items.source_evidence: visitSelectInst rebuilds a select recognized by matchSelectPattern, then casts back to the original select type. The pattern recognizer admits floating min/max forms as well as integer forms; the inventory lists fcmp and FP casts.
items.capability_gap: Floating compare/minmax transformations require NaN, signed-zero, poisoned-float, and potentially fast-math semantics that Puddle does not provide (capability guide lines 31-33 and 166-173).
items.recommended_scope: Keep integer min/max/abs select-pattern cases pending where their exact compare and casts are scalar integer operations. Apply the blocker to FP patterns only.

items.source_evidence: The branch recognizes NOT of either ICmp or FCmp and changes the comparison predicate to its inverse; it uses one-use or freely-invert-all-users as a graph/profitability condition.
items.capability_gap: FCmp predicate inversion needs floating NaN/poison semantics absent from Puddle. LLVM ICmp `samesign` is also not represented in `IcmpProperties` (guide lines 95-98).
items.recommended_scope: Keep scalar integer ICmp inversion pending for flag-free comparisons; do not treat one-use/profitability or the all-user helper as a semantic blocker. Explicitly scope out FCmp and comparisons with samesign.

items.source_evidence: The matched chain is NOT(BitCast(one-use comparison)); it mutates the comparison predicate and returns a bitcast of the comparison.
items.capability_gap: The meaningful bitcast case requires a vector comparison result viewed through a different bit shape; vector integer operations have no elementwise proof interface and FCmp additionally needs unavailable FP semantics. A scalar i1 comparison bitcast to i1 is a no-op case, not the nontrivial source transform.
items.recommended_scope: Treat the substantive source family as vector/FP-blocked. Do not claim a nontrivial scalar integer specialization unless a distinct legal scalar bitcast shape is established.
items.coordinator_resolution: The useful nontrivial forms are vector/FP, but that does not exclude the scalar i1-to-i1 bitcast form: the pinned LLVM CastInst::castIsValid accepts equal-width non-pointer casts and the InstCombine branch has no distinct-type guard. Restored the modeled scalar ICmp specialization to pending, retaining vector/FP limitations.

items.source_evidence: For NOT of a one-use select, the branch inverts ICmp/FCmp predicates or flips constant arms, then returns the select.
items.capability_gap: FCmp-arm inversion requires unsupported floating compare semantics; integer ICmp `samesign` is absent from the dialect property model (guide lines 95-98).
items.recommended_scope: Keep scalar integer compare/constant-arm variants pending for flag-free ICmp. Block only FP arms and samesign-bearing ICmps; do not block on the one-use profitability guard.

items.source_evidence: foldVectorBinop explicitly requires vector type, folds constant vector.insert and splat operands, and rebuilds vector.insert.
items.capability_gap: Vector integer/floating constant semantics lack an elementwise proof interface; the source additionally permits floating binops, whose FP semantics are unavailable (capability guide lines 31-33, 166-173).
items.recommended_scope: This helper branch is vector-only; blocker applies to its entire substantive transformation. Keep separate scalar binop inventory entries unaffected.

items.source_evidence: The constructor creates a vector binop with copied IR flags and wraps it in llvm.vector.reverse; callers match vector-reverse/splat shapes.
items.capability_gap: No vector elementwise proof interface and no llvm.vector.reverse Puddle opcode/interpreter case; floating binops further require FP semantics.
items.recommended_scope: The constructed result is necessarily vector-valued, so this source outcome is blocked as a whole. Do not propagate that blocker to scalar binop folds.

items.source_evidence: The constructor creates a vector binop, all-true vector mask, and llvm.experimental.vp.reverse call with EVL.
items.capability_gap: Puddle has no vector elementwise semantics or VP reverse/mask/EVL semantics; FP variants also exceed the FP model.
items.recommended_scope: This is a vector-only constructed outcome and is blocked as a whole. Keep scalar callers/folds separately scoped.

screened_not_recommendations.note: The opcode list contains fcmp as a broad candidate artifact, but pinned source uses an integer ICmp NE after the NUW trunc test; no FP blocker is warranted.
These call or synthesize scalar integer intrinsics that the guide explicitly lists as modeled. Intrinsic CallInst spelling alone is not a capability gap.
Funnel shifts and freeze are represented scalar integer operations; no unsupported semantic gap was identified for the scalar branch.

These are PHI helper-delegation sites with mixed opcode families, not independent rewrite counts. Any FP/vector blocker belongs on the concrete delegated outcome after helper classification, not on generic delegation merely because its opcode list is broad.
